item.title: Smart Battery Charging Safety Hub - Hackster.io
item.description:
요약

  • Battery-powered devices are widely used in everyday life, but improper charging, excessive temperature, abnorma
  • The Smart Battery Health Monitoring System is an IoT-based prototype designed to continuously monitor important battery parameters and identify potentially unsafe charging conditions.
  • The system combines an Arduino Nano 33 IoT with a Raspberry Pi 4 to collect sensor readings, analyse battery conditions, communicate data through MQTT and display real-time information on a web-based dashboard.

본문

Battery-powered devices are widely used in everyday life, but improper charging, excessive temperature, abnorma

l current flow and potentially hazardous gas emissions can create safety risks.

The Smart Battery Health Monitoring System is an IoT-based prototype designed to continuously monitor important battery parameters and identify potentially unsafe charging conditions.

The system combines an Arduino Nano 33 IoT with a Raspberry Pi 4 to collect sensor readings, analyse battery conditions, communicate data through MQTT and display real-time information on a web-based dashboard.

It aims to provide continuous monitoring, early warning alerts and automated safety responses.

Traditional battery charging systems often provide limited information about the battery's operating conditions. Users may not be aware of abnormal temperature, current fluctuations or potentially dangerous environmental conditions until a problem becomes noticeable.

We wanted to develop a system that goes beyond basic monitoring by combining multiple sensors, intelligent risk assessment and automated responses.

Our goal was to create an affordable prototype that could make battery charging safer, more transparent and easier to monitor.

3. System Architecture

The system consists of two main processing units:

Arduino Nano 33 IoT: Collects sensor readings and handles the local hardware monitoring and safety-control functions.

Raspberry Pi 4: Receives monitoring data, processes it and supports the dashboard and communication services.

The overall data flow is:

Sensors → Arduino Nano 33 IoT → Raspberry Pi 4 → MQTT → Flask Dashboard → Monitoring and Safety Response.

MQTT enables communication between the hardware and software components, allowing sensor information and system status to be displayed in real time.

4. Hardware Components

The prototype uses the following components:

Arduino Nano 33 IoT

- Arduino Nano 33 IoT

- Raspberry Pi 4

ACS712 current sensor

- ACS712 current sensor

0–25V voltage sensor module

- 0–25V voltage sensor module

MQ-2 gas and smoke sensor

- MQ-2 gas and smoke sensor

NTC 10K thermistor

- NTC 10K thermistor

Red, green and yellow LEDs

- Red, green and yellow LEDs

Battery and connecting wires

- Battery and connecting wires

Each sensor monitors a different parameter:

Current sensor: Measures current flowing through the monitored circuit.

Voltage sensor: Measures battery voltage.

- Voltage sensor: Measures battery voltage.

MQ-2 sensor: Detects changes in gas and smoke levels.

NTC thermistor: Monitors temperature changes.

- NTC thermistor: Monitors temperature changes.

The relay, LEDs and buzzer provide hardware-level control and warning indications.

The software side of the project uses:

Arduino IDE and C++ for microcontroller programming.

Python on Raspberry Pi for data processing.

- Python on Raspberry Pi for data processing.

MQTT for communication between system components.

- MQTT for communication between system components.

Flask for the web-based monitoring dashboard.

item.description:
요약

  • The harder work is keeping lighting, focus and magnification consistent across workstations and leaving final quality calls with trained operators.
  • When many sample types need only five to 10 labeled images per class, model building gets cheap, and consistent lighting, focus and magnification become the main thing a quality lab has to control.

본문

Leica pitches offline microscope AI trained on 5–10 images

Leica Microsystems' Aivaro AI Feature Detection, a licensed add-on to its Enersight microscope software, runs without internet access. Many samples need only five to 10 labeled images per class. The harder work is keeping lighting, focus and magnification consistent across workstations and leaving final quality calls with trained operators.

This story was produced through MarketScale. See how Industrial IoT teams put it to work with AI Visibility (GEO).

When many sample types need only five to 10 labeled images per class, model building gets cheap, and consistent lighting, focus and magnification become the main thing a quality lab has to control.

Fully offline AI inspection now appears in products as different as Leica's microscope module and preML's inline camera kit, which gives buyers solid ground to ask for it on lines that handle proprietary work.

Any AI inspection pilot should count false rejects and defect escapes separately; a single accuracy figure can hide a shift from one to the other.

Turn your Industrial IoT expertise into content.

Record interviews, organize footage, and write with AI on a free trial of the MarketScale platform for qualifying companies. No demo required, no credit card.

On a densely populated printed circuit board, a scratch can disappear into the traces, pads and surface texture around it. Leica Microsystems, a Danaher company, has built a module for the microscopes that hunt for such scratches: Aivaro AI Feature Detection, a separately licensed add-on to its Enersight software platform for digital microscopes and cameras. In a Nov. 23 article in Laser Focus World, Leica senior commercial product manager Marjus Seubert described software that finds, classifies, counts and measures defects, inclusions and particles in live or captured images, then saves the results with the image so they can go straight into a report.

Two of Leica's claims matter most to a quality lab manager. For many sample types, a model needs only five to 10 labeled images per class. And the software runs on standard hardware with no cloud connection or internet access. Put those together and the effort in an AI inspection project lands somewhere new.

Cheap models mean the discipline around the microscope carries the project.

From a handful of images to a model

Leica starts each task from pre-trained models and fine-tunes them where the images are captured, an approach it calls edge learning. Users mark the features that matter with a magic wand tool, a Quick Selection brush or freehand drawing. Once trained, the model can count what it finds and report minimum, maximum and average measurements. One example image in Leica's article shows the minimum Feret diameter calculated for each feature detected in a cross-section.

item.title: Home Assistant with no Wi-Fi or Bluetooth? Here's how it works - How-To Geek
item.description:
요약

  • Today, we're looking at a setup for your Home Assistant that doesn't rely on Wi-Fi or Bluetooth.
  • The name of the project is Dumb Devices, and the user peterisza released it on the Home Assistant community forum.
  • You'll still need to load the firmware onto the boards, fit them into their enclosures, and then wire each device into the 24-volt bus. Once you've connected the bus to your Home Assistant computer through the USB controller, the devices should show up automatically.

본문

Today, we're looking at a setup for your Home Assistant that doesn't rely on Wi-Fi or Bluetooth. The name of the project is Dumb Devices, and the user peterisza released it on the Home Assistant community forum. The project has the goal of taking the "I" out of IoT, which goes against the philosophy manufacturers normally follow when they make IoT devices.

Isza makes the case that instead of relying on internet connectivity, you can wire your devices together with no Wi-Fi, Cloud, pairing, or registration. The project has several prototypes currently available, but be warned: it may require more user input than a simple IoT device setup, and they're not quite ready for use.

Dumb Devices: Home Assistant without internet is possible

Could this end up being an alternative to IoT devices?

Isza created several prototypes to prove the point, including LED drivers, a relay, a heating valve controller, and a touch panel that measures humidity, temperature, and CO2 levels. The only smart device that you need is a home assistant to control everything. Since IoT devices are historically invasive and easier to hack, the project could potentially be a huge improvement to home security.

They all connect to the same 3-wire 24-volt bus, which connects directly to your home assistant through a USB controller. The connection is automatic once you plug in the USB controller. Isza designed the hardware itself so that a small installer can send the files to a manufacturer, who assembles the boards and then sends them back to you.

"All the manufacturing comes down to a few-click order from JLCPCB, IN3DTEC, etc. So no soldering, no hunting down parts, no building. Mostly you can just order the electronics and the enclosure, upload the firmware, and boom, you have the device," Isza explains.

"Mostly" does the heavy lifting in his explanation but also reveals that there will be some manual user setup and maintenance. You'll still need to load the firmware onto the boards, fit them into their enclosures, and then wire each device into the 24-volt bus. Once you've connected the bus to your Home Assistant computer through the USB controller, the devices should show up automatically.

Despite the setup, Isza wants the project to be accessible; Isza put the cost at roughly $8 to $15 per device in a batch of 30 devices. Depending on your devices and setup and how many you're ordering in bulk, the cost may be higher. The bigger idea is that if a relay dies years after the project goes quiet, someone could use the same open manufacturing files to order a replacement.

"The goal is that small companies and installers can “manufacture” (in reality basically just order) these devices for themselves and obtain them at a low cost, at 0% manufacturer margin and 0% distributor margin," Isza explains.

item.title: 450MHz Alliance expands to boost networks in critical infrastructure - Computer Weekly
item.description:
요약

  • Kornkanok - stock.adobe.com
  • IoT connectivity provider joins association representing stakeholders providing tech in key wireless spectrum rage as NR+ extends private cellular networks to the grid edge
  • For its part, IoT connectivity firm Wirepas looks to deliver the invisible infrastructure behind ultra-resilient, infinitely scalable mesh networks for large-scale, mission-critical industrial and commercial deployments.

본문

Kornkanok - stock.adobe.com

450MHz Alliance expands to boost networks in critical infrastructure

IoT connectivity provider joins association representing stakeholders providing tech in key wireless spectrum rage as NR+ extends private cellular networks to the grid edge

As it continues with its mission to advance cellular and mesh wireless communications technologies in utilities and similar infrastructure applications, resilient, scalable connectivity provider Wirepas has joined the 450MHz Alliance, the non-profit industry group of utilities, equipment makers and operators promoting the spectrum band, to support hybrid private cellular and mesh networks for critical infrastructure.

450MHz Alliance is an industry association representing stakeholders in the 450MHz spectrum, and has the stated mission of promoting the potential of the key spectrum band and helping its members achieve their objectives more effectively. The members of the alliance include wireless carriers, equipment manufacturers and companies in various vertical markets for machine-to-machine communication.

Among its principal functions are representation in industry and regulatory bodies; promotion and growth of the 450MHz band and its ecosystem; facilitating coordination in supply and demand of 450MHz equipment and terminals; driving the economies of scale; taking regulatory positions; setting the industry standard; and supporting development and advocacy of new business models.

As an example of how the band is being used, in September 2026, Aramco Digital announced it had expanded its mission-critical connectivity services and connected digital capabilities in industrial sectors and large-scale operating environments across Saudi Arabia using managed communications services over the 450MHz network.

This included expanded network coverage, mission-critical push-to-talk offerings, connected devices, telecommunications services, and internet of things (IoT) and artificial intelligence products.

For its part, IoT connectivity firm Wirepas looks to deliver the invisible infrastructure behind ultra-resilient, infinitely scalable mesh networks for large-scale, mission-critical industrial and commercial deployments. Its product, the Wirepas Platform, is based on the principles of the NR+ wireless standard.

Wirepas said private cellular networks offer utilities wide-area coverage and full control over their critical communications. It regards mesh technology as being able to extend private cellular networks to the last mile, connecting devices beyond the direct reach of cellular coverage. Conversely, it noted that cellular can provide reach and backhaul connectivity to support mesh deployments – for example, in dense urban environments.

요약

  • - DataPrint will distribute Kerlink’s full range of Wirnet indoor and outdoor LoRaWAN gateways in France and promote Kerlink’s deployment, security and network operations services.
  • - The partnership pairs Kerlink’s gateways and services with DataPrint’s LoRaWAN sensor range to offer complete IoT solutions for smart buildings, smart cities and industrial IoT.
  • IoT solutions specialist Kerlink entered into a distribution partnership with DataPrint that extends Kerlink’s market coverage in France and reinforces its ecosystem of trusted distribution partners.

본문

- DataPrint will distribute Kerlink’s full range of Wirnet indoor and outdoor LoRaWAN gateways in France and promote Kerlink’s deployment, security and network operations services.

- The partnership pairs Kerlink’s gateways and services with DataPrint’s LoRaWAN sensor range to offer complete IoT solutions for smart buildings, smart cities and industrial IoT.

IoT solutions specialist Kerlink entered into a distribution partnership with DataPrint that extends Kerlink’s market coverage in France and reinforces its ecosystem of trusted distribution partners.

Under the terms of the partnership, DataPrint will distribute Kerlink’s full portfolio of LoRaWAN gateways, including both the Wirnet indoor and outdoor ranges. In addition to providing hardware, DataPrint will promote Kerlink’s expert-backed services designed to help customers deploy, secure, and operate their LoRaWAN® networks faster and with greater confidence.

The partnership allows Kerlink and DataPrint to jointly cover the entire IoT value chain— gateways and services from Kerlink, combined with DataPrint’s broad range of LoRaWAN® sensors— to deliver complete solutions and extend field coverage nationwide. It is designed to accelerate growth in key IoT markets, including smart buildings, smart cities, and industrial IoT, by leveraging DataPrint’s ecosystem and market expertise.

What Does the Kerlink and DataPrint Partnership Mean for IoT Customers?

William Gouesbet, Kerlink CEO, stated the partnership gives their customers access to complete IoT solutions, from sensors to gateways to services, all in one place.

“That’s what makes it so valuable, it’s not just about combining hardware: it’s about pairing DataPrint’s reach and sensor range with the expertise behind Kerlink’s own services, so customers can deploy, secure, and operate their networks faster and with greater confidence,” said Gousbet in a statement. “With the LoRaWAN market accelerating, we’re confident this alliance positions us to grow even faster.”

Why Kerlink Chose DataPrint to Grow LoRaWAN in France

Kerlink’s channel strategy aims to build a worldwide ecosystem of trusted distribution partners capable of serving customers locally. DataPrint’s strong position in the French IoT market, together with its recognized expertise in IoT solutions, makes it a natural fit for this approach.

The agreement further enhances the level of technical support available to end-customers, with the ultimate goal of increasing LoRaWAN business volumes in France.

Officials highlighted that that partnership reflects Kerlink’s confidence in the continued growth of IoT and LoRaWAN deployments across France, particularly in smart-building applications such as energy monitoring and utility submetering. As customers increasingly expect end-to-end solutions combining gateways, sensors, connectivity, and support services, DataPrint’s one-stop-shop model aligns closely with this market trend.

item.title: Roaming vendors gear up for 5G standalone and satellite connectivity - IOT Insider
item.description:
요약

  • Roaming providers are preparing for the expansion of 5G standalone (5G SA) and satellite connectivity, as mobile operators look to strengthen their international services and adapt to changing demands for global connectivity.
  • The company’s 2026-2027 Roaming Vendor Hub evaluated more than 190 product offerings across 10 categories, including IPX, roaming hubs, steering of roaming, fraud management, signalling security, clearing and settlement, and travel eSIM services.
  • The research, which involved more than five months of product demonstrations, questionnaires, interviews and company briefings, identified 23 Champion vendors across the different categories.

본문

Roaming providers are preparing for the expansion of 5G standalone (5G SA) and satellite connectivity, as mobile operators look to strengthen their international services and adapt to changing demands for global connectivity.

A new assessment of 85 roaming vendors and wholesale providers by telecoms research firm Kaleido Intelligence highlights how suppliers are positioning their portfolios to meet these requirements, alongside growing interest in artificial intelligence (AI), network security and roaming analytics.

The company’s 2026-2027 Roaming Vendor Hub evaluated more than 190 product offerings across 10 categories, including IPX, roaming hubs, steering of roaming, fraud management, signalling security, clearing and settlement, and travel eSIM services.

The research, which involved more than five months of product demonstrations, questionnaires, interviews and company briefings, identified 23 Champion vendors across the different categories. A further 33 suppliers were recognised as High Flyers.

Kaleido Intelligence said the results reflected a market in which operators are balancing demand for broader service portfolios with the need for specialist technologies to address specific technical challenges.

“Our latest Vendor Hub results show how roaming vendors and suppliers are responding to operators’ changing priorities, from applying AI in roaming operations to supporting the rollout of 5G standalone roaming,” said Nitin Bhas, Chief of Strategy & Insights at Kaleido Intelligence. “We saw strong performances from vendors with broad portfolios and from specialists tackling specific technical challenges.”

Among the category leaders, Cellusys retained its top position in Steering of Roaming for the fourth consecutive year, while Comfone was named the leading Champion provider in Roaming Hubs. Orange Wholesale secured recognition in Sponsored Roaming, and Telna retained its leading position in Travel eSIM while also achieving Champion status in Sponsored Roaming.

Syniverse recorded the highest overall score across all 10 product categories for the sixth consecutive year. It was also named the leading Champion vendor in IPX and Data & Financial Clearing. BICS, Orange Wholesale and Vodafone Procure & Connect also achieved strong overall scores, reflecting the breadth of their roaming portfolios.

The findings point to the importance of established roaming infrastructure as operators prepare to support new connectivity models. The expansion of 5G standalone roaming and satellite services will bring additional requirements for interconnection, network management and visibility across increasingly complex international networks.

He added that the company’s investment in next-generation solutions was intended to give operators greater insight as roaming expands into 5G standalone and satellite connectivity.
